test-in-motion.footage: An attempt you can recognize in one frame, with the rule visible beside the action.
test-in-motion.check: Freeze the first frame. Can someone tell what the person is trying to do, and what would count as success?

proof-first.footage: A striking finished shot and a source frame that shares its subject, gesture or camera angle.
proof-first.check: Cut from the result to the source with the sound off. The viewer should still recognize the same moment.

live-contradiction.footage: One uninterrupted view where a visible event overturns an easy first guess.
live-contradiction.check: Keep a fixed edge, scale or landmark in frame through the surprise so a hidden cut cannot explain it.

impossible-move.footage: Two states you can join on the same moving hand, silhouette or foreground edge.
impossible-move.check: Step through the join. Its screen position, travel direction and speed should agree across both shots.

character-collision.footage: Two roles with different aims, a shared object and a clean sightline for each role.
character-collision.check: Mute the exchange. Each change of speaker should still be legible from position, eyeline or interaction.

reaction-first.footage: A genuine reaction and the specific event that prompted it, captured in the same encounter.
reaction-first.check: Return to the full moment. The expression and what caused it should have the same meaning in context.

object-reveal.footage: An object someone can open, rotate or expose, plus the first job the hidden part actually does.
object-reveal.check: Pause on the first close-up. The viewer should be able to locate the part in the original object.

specific-fix.footage: A repeatable fault, one visible adjustment, and the same test after the change.
specific-fix.check: Play both tests at the same size, speed and volume. The improvement should survive that comparison.

choice-live.footage: Two viable options and an observable tap, answer or action that commits to one of them.
choice-live.check: Advance the score only after the commitment. Viewers should know which rule earned the point.

turning-point.footage: A decision or interruption that immediately changes the next thing someone can do.
turning-point.check: Cut the explanatory line for a test viewing. The consequence should still make the decision understandable.

result-first.footage: A finished result that performs its real job, plus evidence of the earlier state that explains it.
result-first.check: Hold through one complete use. A viewer should be able to say what worked before you cut back.

visible-problem.footage: A failure you can reproduce and a first diagnostic step that could plausibly explain it.
visible-problem.check: Let the failure happen in context. The viewer should be able to describe the symptom before hearing your theory.

learning-promise.footage: A finished skill exercise, its starting material and a working view that lets viewers follow along.
learning-promise.check: After the opening, ask a viewer what they will make and what they would do first.

head-to-head.footage: Two real options tested against the same decision criterion under comparable conditions.
head-to-head.check: Match scale, playback level and exposure wherever they affect the choice. Identify any condition you cannot match.

prediction.footage: A legible setup, two plausible outcomes and a recorded test under the setup you introduce.
prediction.check: A viewer should have time to choose before a sound, cutaway or caption reveals the answer.

mystery.footage: A specific clue and a first line of inquiry that can actually test an explanation.
mystery.check: Keep the clue visible long enough to locate it on the object, document or shot it came from.

evidence-led-reversal.footage: An initial claim, its original basis and a new result that changes how far the claim can go.
evidence-led-reversal.check: Check the dates, units and population on both pieces of evidence. State exactly which part of the claim changes.

constraint-challenge.footage: A goal with a fixed limit on time, material or attempts, plus evidence of the first action that spends it.
constraint-challenge.check: Pause after the first attempt. A viewer should be able to count what has been used and what is left.

decisive-moment.footage: A recorded preparation that leads into a consequential event, with earlier material that explains the stakes.
decisive-moment.check: Mark your return point before cutting away. When you resume, time and action should continue honestly from it.

rare-access.footage: Permission to film a place or operation, a participant who knows it, and something only that viewpoint reveals.
rare-access.check: Show one specific operation and its effect. Identify a rehearsal, reconstruction or sample display when one is used.

personal-stakes.footage: A person who can say what matters to them and a first decision that makes the consequence visible.
personal-stakes.check: Keep enough of the original line for the person to recognize their own meaning. Show what their choice changes.
